summary: Offboarding with third-party leased laptop: custody, KMS keys, and cross-border shipping policy clarification
description:
Issue summary: New offboarding request for a senior engineer (contractor) who has a company provisioned, third-party leased laptop that is physically located in Singapore. HR and Finance have flagged the device because: 1) lease is through a local vendor (vendor contract requires return to Singapore address), 2) the user has access to production service accounts and S3 buckets encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, and 3) the employee is requesting the option to either return the laptop to the vendor (preferred by vendor) or hand it to a local Redwood rep in the US for shipment back to the vendor.

Impact: Risk of unauthorized access if device is not properly wiped and KMS access is not rotated. Potential legal/compliance implications (export controls, local contract terms) depending on shipping choice. HR needs a safe, repeatable process and policy clarification for similar future cases.

Environment: Remote contractor account (internal user), prod credentials present on device, lease vendor: TechLease APAC Pty Ltd (Singapore), KMS: redwood-customer-cmk-01.

Requested outcome: Clear step-by-step offboarding checklist for leased hardware located outside the US and a single recommended flow (vendor return vs Redwood-handback) plus required timeline and owners. Also confirm required KMS rotation scope and whether a targeted rekey (service-account-only) is acceptable or full-customer-CMK rotation is required.
steps_to_complete: Confirm whether vendor contract allows direct handoff to Redwood courier or requires vendor-managed return
If vendor-return required: obtain vendor RMA instructions and authorized return address for Singapore
If Redwood-handback allowed: coordinate with Ops for secure pickup and international shipment (customs, export paperwork)
Inventory device: serial, asset tag, lease ID; verify any customer data footprints (local caches, docker volumes)
Revoke all service account tokens and rotate short-lived API keys associated with the user
Perform device wipe: create ephemeral audit session to verify wipe (Corp IT to run MDM wipe command and capture logs)
KMS plan: propose either targeted rekey for affected service keys or full CMK rotation; include rollback/fallback and expected blast radius
Document final owner of the device chain-of-custody and update asset inventory and lease records
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 — HR (Priya Singh): Contractor notice received; contract end 2026-03-20. Vendor lease docs attached in HR system. Need recommended next steps — do we coordinate pickup?
2026-03-12 10:02 — Security (Lina Gomez): Flagging KMS access. We need answers on which service accounts were used on that machine and whether any long-lived credentials are present.

2026-03-12 11:40 — Reporter (Jordan Patel): Confirmed user had AWS CLI profiles for prod and a local vault agent that pointed to /etc/redwood/vault-token. No evidence yet of custom S3 objects; will request a disk inventory from the user before deprovisioning.

2026-03-12 15:18 — IT Ops (Marcos Rivera): I can coordinate pickup if Redwood is allowed to hand the device to our courier. Need vendor contract snippet or email approval from vendor. Otherwise we should request vendor-managed return and ask HR to share RMA instructions.

2026-03-13 08:07 — Legal (Evelyn Park): Vendor contract clause 6.2 says returns should be to the vendor facility; transfers to third parties need written approval. Putting this in the ticket so HR and Finance can request the vendor's written exception if needed.

2026-03-13 12:33 — HR (Priya Singh): Reached out to vendor for written exception — vendor replied they can accept third-party courier if they receive a signed authorization form. Vendor sent form link.

2026-03-13 14:50 — Security (Lina Gomez): For KMS, recommended approach: rotate any customer-managed data-encryption keys used for service accounts that the contractor had access to. Propose targeted rekey and revoke user IAM principals first; escalate to full CMK rotation only if key access is suspected to be compromised.
investigation_notes: Checked asset inventory: lease ID TL-APAC-7782 matches contractor record; current assigned shipping address is Singapore office (user's home).

Disk inventory request sent to user: user provided list of installed packages and home dir usage; found ~/.aws/credentials with two profiles and /var/lib/docker volumes with built images. No large customer data blobs reported but needs full disk image scan if vendor requests evidence.
Examined IAM logs: contractor principal made routine API calls in last 30 days; no anomalous data exfil patterns found in S3 access logs so far (scan window: last 90 days).
Legal notes: cross-border shipment will require commercial invoice indicating lease return and may trigger VAT paperwork; Ops to include this in shipment manifest.
resolution: Pending — vendor provided authorization form which HR completed 2026-03-13. Next steps: Ops to schedule pickup (Marcos), IT to perform MDM wipe immediately after handoff, Security to revoke user IAM principals and rotate affected service keys (targeted rekey). Assigned owners: Marcos Rivera (pickup & shipping), Lina Gomez (KMS & IAM rotation plan), Priya Singh (vendor liaison and lease closure). Expected closure date: 2026-03-19.
